### Executive Summary
Command injection vulnerabilities have been identified in TP-Link Archer series routers. These flaws enable remote attackers to perform arbitrary code execution on target devices.

Successful exploitation grants high-privilege access to the router hardware. Additional context regarding active exploitation or specific affected model versions is not yet confirmed.

### Technical Impact & Root Cause
The root cause involves command injection flaws present within the TP-Link Archer firmware. Improper input sanitization allows injected commands to pass directly to the device's operating system shell.

The technical impact includes full compromise of the device, allowing arbitrary code execution at the root level. Detailed technical breakdowns of the vulnerability mechanism are not yet confirmed.

### Mitigation & IOCs
Concrete vendor mitigation steps and patch availability are not yet confirmed in the provided source. Administrators should consult official TP-Link support advisories for applicable firmware updates.
